lesson.title: Return Past the Net Player
lesson.hook: The net player looks ready to pounce. You still have a crosscourt lane to the server. Don’t let their presence choose your return.
lesson.liveIntro: The net player looks ready to pounce. You still have a crosscourt lane to the server. Don’t let their presence choose your return.

drA.name: What does this next ball call for?
drA.sit: Your pair has reorganised. Read this contact before trying to finish.
drA.q: What does this next ball call for?
opts: Use controlled depth through the middle

lines.A: You give the ball room and prepare together for another reply.
lines.B: It lands here, but the smaller target leaves less margin. Keep covering.

drA.take: Read the net player. Return through the available space.
drA.payoff: Read the net player. Return through the available space.
drA.principle: Read the net player. Return through the available space.
drA.why: A crosscourt return often gives a useful lane away from the opposing net player. Watch the actual position: a player moving across can change that choice. Your partner must also adjust for the next hitter.

pro.label: Cayer · Pressure changes the net player
pro.moment: Louis Cayer, coach to doubles world No.1s, explains that a net player can squeeze towards the middle when the opponent is under pressure. Their position changes the returner’s space.
pro.read: Your next point: look at where the net player is, not just where you normally return. Use a lane the actual position leaves available.

drill.name: Rehearse as a pair
drill.how: Serve ten practice points. The net player sometimes holds and sometimes moves across. Returners name the lane they saw; both partners recover for the reply.
